answers.how: Fitting the ball's vertical trajectory gives about 553 px/s², so 1 px corresponds to 1.77 cm. Its diameter is approximately 12.5 px.
The middle person's head-to-foot height is approximately 99 px; the gravity-derived scale is 1.77 cm/px.
The passer measures approximately 85 px head-to-foot when upright, multiplied by 1.77 cm/px.
The receiver's initial head-to-foot height is approximately 99 px, multiplied by 1.77 cm/px.
The initial horizontal separation is approximately 248 px. The trajectory calibration gives 0.0177 m/px.
At 1.00 s, the fitted trajectory gives horizontal and vertical velocity components of approximately 1.96 and 2.88 m/s; their vector magnitude is 3.48 m/s.
The ball's horizontal position changes at approximately 111 px/s, multiplied by the gravity-derived scale of 0.0177 m/px.
